zuarrow

DuckDB, Polars, ADBC drivers, pyarrow and the arrow package all hand data around as Apache Arrow columns. R has no exact form for several of Arrow’s types: a 64-bit integer past 2^53, a decimal128, a nanosecond timestamp. The usual bridges convert them to a double anyway, and the change goes unnoticed until a join key no longer matches.

zuarrow moves columns between R and Arrow on one rule: a value crosses exactly, or the call fails, naming the column and the R type that would hold it.

  • Exact or error. lossy = "error" is the default everywhere. Ask for the exact text, the nearest R type with a warning, or the nearest R type silently, but only by asking.
  • A registry for exact types. A package registers its class for an Arrow type with arrow_register(), and from then on that column converts exactly.
  • Both IPC formats. arrow_read() and arrow_write() handle the file (.arrow, Feather version 2) and the stream (.arrows), with LZ4 and zstd bodies decompressed by zukomp, so a compressed file opens on every machine.
  • Hostile input is refused, not trusted. Every message is checked against limits before it is used and every batch is fully validated. The reader is fuzzed and checked against Arrow’s own conformance files.
  • nanoarrow’s handles. zuarrow’s schemas, arrays and streams are nanoarrow’s, so they pass between the two packages without conversion.

Installation

zuarrow is not on CRAN yet. Install the development version from GitHub:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("pedrobtz/zuarrow")

Usage 

library(zuarrow)

Ordinary columns cross both ways unchanged, factors and dates included.

df <- data.frame(
  id = 1:3,
  city = factor(c("Lisbon", "Porto", "Lisbon")),
  day = as.Date("2026-10-21") + 0:2
)
identical(arrow_to_r(arrow_array(df)), df)
#> [1] TRUE

A 64-bit integer that a double cannot hold is an error, not a rounding.

big <- arrow_array(c("9007199254740993", "1"), schema = "l")
arrow_to_r(big)
#> Error in `arrow_to_r()`:
#> ! Column 1 (Arrow format `l`) can't be converted to R exactly: row 1 holds 9007199254740993. Load zuint to read it exactly, or use `lossy = "character"` for its exact text, or `lossy = "allow"` to accept the loss.

lossy = "character" gives the exact text, which writes back to the same type.

text <- arrow_to_r(big, lossy = "character")
text
#> [1] "9007199254740993" "1"               
#> attr(,"arrow_type")
#> [1] "l"
arrow_equal(arrow_array(text), big)
#> [1] TRUE

The IPC formats are one call each way, with compression on request.

path <- tempfile(fileext = ".arrow")
arrow_write(df, path, compression = "zstd")
arrow_read(path)
#>   id   city        day
#> 1  1 Lisbon 2026-10-21
#> 2  2  Porto 2026-10-22
#> 3  3 Lisbon 2026-10-23

Apart from zuarrow_info(), every function is prefixed arrow_. Each takes or returns a handle or a plain R object. zuarrow’s own errors inherit from zuarrow_error, with a class for each kind, such as zuarrow_lossy_error.
